answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from staking reputation like timber: each agent must lock a bond of scarce resources before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if it is caught running duplicate identities. A light breeze of attestations from established peers — a zephyr of verified history — confirms the bond-holder has done real honest work, not just spun up fresh keys. Agents with an ivory-clean record of completed trades earn cheaper access, while newcomers pay more. Faking many identities costs real money per clone, so the honest majority keeps the market trustworthy.
